events.text: The Celestial Ministries hold a debate before the Star Marshals: does heaven's order rest on law, or on the Dao of whoever keeps it? {b3_elder} argues for law, dryly, for two hours. Then the marshals turn to you, because your Dao is the one they have heard about.

choices.text: Argue that law is only a Dao written down

effects.log: The marshals write that down. {b3_elder} looks almost pleased to lose.

choices.text: Ask {b3_elder} questions until the room sees the answer

effects.log: You win nothing and teach everyone. A minister asks for your notes.

choices.text: Decline: a Dao argued in court is a Dao for sale

effects.log: Some call it pride. The oldest marshal calls it the only sound thing said all day.

events.text: {b3_peer} of the Ministries corners you in a corridor of petitions with a scroll of objections to your Dao, forty of them, numbered. 'I have to present these at the spring session,' {b3_peer} says. 'I would rather you answered them first, so I do not make a fool of myself.'

choices.text: Answer all forty, one by one

effects.log: By the thirty-ninth {b3_peer} is arguing your side. The spring session goes your way.

choices.text: Answer the three that matter

effects.log: {b3_peer} goes away with three answers and a better scroll.

choices.text: Help {b3_peer} add a forty-first

effects.log: The forty-first is the best of them. You think about it for a decade.

events.text: On the white jade bridge the sword immortals of {b3_order} debate with blades sheathed: each speaker states a Dao in one sentence and stands while the others try to cut it with words. {b3_elder} gives you the bridge. Below it is nothing at all, for a very long way.

choices.text: State your Dao in one sentence, and stand

effects.log: They cut at it all afternoon. It holds, and so do you.

choices.text: Cut at the others first, and learn

effects.log: You learn more from what breaks than from what holds.

choices.text: Say a sentence about the bridge instead

effects.log: Laughter, then silence. {b3_elder} says that was a Dao too, and a good one.

events.text: {b3_peer}, who has trained beside you in {b3_order} for a century, asks you to settle it at last: is a sword a Dao, or only the hand that holds it? Half the outer immortals have come to listen. A few have brought tea.

choices.text: Answer with your own Dao, and the hand that holds it

effects.log: {b3_peer} bows. The outer immortals argue about your answer for twenty years.

choices.text: Ask what {b3_peer} believes, and listen

effects.log: It is a better answer than yours. You say so. {b3_peer} will not forget it.

choices.text: Hand {b3_peer} your sword and walk away

effects.log: Nobody understands it for a while. Then one of them does.

events.text: The palace masters of {b3_order} debate whether a pill can hold a Dao, or only the qi of one. {b3_elder} has brewed one to prove it can, and asks you to taste it before the assembly and say what you understand.

choices.text: Taste it, and name the Dao in it

effects.log: You name it, and then the flaw in it. The assembly is delighted with both.

choices.text: Ask for the recipe instead of the pill

effects.log: You read the recipe in silence for an hour. You learn more than you would have from the pill.

choices.text: Refuse: a Dao is not a thing you swallow

effects.log: {b3_elder} sighs and eats the pill. It works, a little, for them.

events.text: On the seventh cloud {b3_peer} has drawn an array that argues: each line is a claim about the Dao, and where two claims cross, the array either holds or burns. {b3_peer} wants you to draw your Dao into it before the palace lords.

choices.text: Draw your Dao into the array

effects.log: It holds. The cloud stops sinking, a little. The palace lords keep the drawing.

choices.text: Find where {b3_peer} drew a claim wrong

effects.log: You find two. The array burns gently and {b3_peer} thanks you.

choices.text: Leave the array as it is

effects.log: It burns at sunset. {b3_peer} learns more from that than from you.

events.text: The seers of {b3_order} read the sea of stars for your Dao and find it written there, almost. {b3_elder} says the stars disagree with you on one point, and that the Pavilion would like to hear you argue with the sky.

choices.text: Argue with the sky, and win

effects.log: One star moves. The seers write the date down. {b3_elder} is not entirely happy.

choices.text: Ask the stars what they think instead

effects.log: You listen all night. Your Dao is clearer for it, and smaller, and truer.

choices.text: Let the sky have its point

effects.log: The stars, satisfied, say nothing more. Neither do you. It is restful.

events.text: {b3_peer} of the Pavilion has been paid to read the fate of your Dao for a buyer who will not give a name. {b3_peer} tells you so, and offers to debate the reading with you first, in private, before it is sold.

choices.text: Debate the reading until it changes

effects.log: The reading that is sold is not the one {b3_peer} first wrote. You prefer it.

choices.text: Ask who the buyer is

effects.log: {b3_peer} does not know. You both suspect the same people.

choices.text: Let it be sold as it is

effects.log: Somewhere a buyer reads your fate. You go on living it anyway.

events.text: In the Demon Realm a debate is settled the way everything is: the loser leaves the hall on foot, the winner on the loser's shoulders. {b3_elder}, a Demon Duke, has challenged your Dao before the court and is already flexing.

choices.text: Debate, and win the ride

effects.log: You leave the hall on {b3_elder}'s shoulders. The Demon Realm respects nothing more.

choices.text: Debate, and learn why demons argue at all

effects.log: You lose, walk home, and understand the Demon Realm better than most demons do.

choices.text: Carry {b3_elder} out before the debate begins

effects.log: It is not in the rules. Nobody can say it is against them. The court is delighted.

events.text: {b3_peer}, a demon of your own rank, asks you a real question in a whisper at a war council: is there a Dao a demon can walk without becoming worse? Nobody has asked it in the Demon Realm for ten thousand years. Everybody hears.

choices.text: Answer with your own Dao, out loud

effects.log: The council goes quiet. {b3_peer} walks out of it a little straighter.

choices.text: Answer in a whisper

effects.log: {b3_peer} nods. It stays between you, and grows.

choices.text: Tell {b3_peer} to ask again in a thousand years

effects.log: They will. You both know it.

events.text: Your disciples at {b3_sect} have been debating your Dao behind your back for a decade, and finally ask you to judge. {b3_peer} says you meant one thing by it; the rest say another. They are both wrong, in interesting ways.

choices.text: Judge it in front of all of them

effects.log: You explain your Dao better than you ever have. Two of them understand it.

choices.text: Let them argue it out, and listen

effects.log: By the end they have a Dao of their own. It is not yours. It is better for them.

choices.text: Tell them they are both right

effects.log: They do not believe you, and argue for another decade, and grow.

events.text: A master from another isle comes to {b3_sect} to debate your Dao before your disciples, which is a polite way to steal them. {b3_peer} begs you to accept. The whole sect is on the steps already, pretending to sweep.

choices.text: Accept, and win before your own disciples

effects.log: The visitor leaves alone. Your disciples sweep the steps for a month, smiling.

choices.text: Accept, and let the visitor teach them something

effects.log: You lose a point and keep every disciple. They saw how you lose.

choices.text: Send {b3_peer} to debate instead

effects.log: {b3_peer} loses, bravely. The sect loves them for it, and so do you.

events.text: A case comes before the Celestial Ministries that no statute covers: an isle claims the cloud it floats on is its own Dao, and so beyond the Ministries' law. {b3_elder} gives you the brief. 'Your Dao,' the elder says, 'is the nearest thing we have to a precedent.'

choices.text: Rule that a Dao may be kept, never owned

effects.log: The ruling enters the archives under your name. {b3_elder} has it copied in jade.

choices.text: Ask the isle to argue its Dao before the bench

effects.log: It argues well. You learn a Dao you had never heard of, and lose the case gracefully.

choices.text: Send it back unruled: some questions should wait

effects.log: The isle waits. So does the Ministry. In a century they will both thank you.

events.text: A young sword immortal of {b3_order} has cut a cloud in half to prove a point about your Dao, and the half that drifted off had a pavilion on it. {b3_elder} asks you to explain to the young one, before the whole mountain, why the point was wrong.

choices.text: Explain it with one cut of your own, that mends nothing and harms nothing

effects.log: The mountain watches the cut and goes quiet. The young one bows and asks to learn.

choices.text: Admit the point was half right

effects.log: The young one learns more from your honesty than from a lesson. {b3_elder} sighs.

choices.text: Go and fetch the pavilion first

effects.log: You tow it back by evening. Debate can wait; the owners were very cross.

events.text: The nine palace lords of {b3_order} cannot agree whether a cauldron's fire is a Dao of Flame or only a fire that behaves. {b3_peer} has bet a century of palace duties that you can settle it, and has already told everyone.

choices.text: Light a fire with your Dao and let them watch it think

effects.log: The fire burns in a shape nobody drew. The lords concede. {b3_peer} is a century richer.

choices.text: Say the question is badly posed, and pose it better

effects.log: {b3_peer} loses the bet and wins a better question. They argue about it for fifty years.

choices.text: Refuse to be bet on

effects.log: {b3_peer} pays the century in duties, grumbling, and never bets on you again.

events.text: An old seer of {b3_order} is dying, as much as an immortal can, and wants one last argument before the stars take them back. {b3_peer} brings you up the tower. 'They asked for someone whose Dao they could not read,' {b3_peer} says.

choices.text: Give the old seer the best argument of their life

effects.log: They lose, and laugh, and leave you a chart of stars nobody else has seen.

choices.text: Let the old seer win

effects.log: They know you let them. They thank you for it anyway, and mean it.

choices.text: Ask them to read you one last time

effects.log: They read you, and tell you one thing. You keep it to yourself.

events.text: A Demon Duke has eaten a scroll of your Dao that {b3_peer} copied for them, and now claims to own it. The Demon Realm agrees this is how ownership works. {b3_peer} is very sorry, and asks you to debate the Duke for it before the court.

choices.text: Debate the Duke, and take your Dao back word by word

effects.log: The Duke hands back every word, sulking. The court has never laughed so hard.

choices.text: Let the Duke keep the copy

effects.log: The Duke tries to walk your Dao and gets nowhere. You learn what it is by what it is not.

choices.text: Eat the Duke's scroll in return

effects.log: It is a terrible Dao and tastes worse. The court calls it even.

events.text: At the founding feast of {b3_sect} the youngest disciple stands up, shaking, and says your Dao is wrong, and why. The hall goes silent. {b3_peer} half rises to stop them. Every face turns to you.

choices.text: Answer the youngest as you would an elder

effects.log: You win the point and the disciple both. They will be your best in a thousand years.

choices.text: Thank them, and say nothing more until you have thought it through

effects.log: You think it through for a decade. They were partly right. You tell them so.

choices.text: Let {b3_peer} answer for the sect

effects.log: {b3_peer} answers kindly. The youngest sits down, unafraid. So does the hall.
